claims.text: A machine-learning framework can rapidly predict RHEA compositions.
The predicted RHEA compositions can simultaneously achieve high strength, superior ductility, and low weight under refractory conditions.
The proposed framework integrates elemental properties, mixing entropy, density, and phase-stability indices.
RHEAs have a vast compositional space because they contain multiple principal elements.
Rapid and targeted design methodologies for RHEAs are currently lacking.
The proposed model would be trained on high-throughput computational and experimental RHEA datasets.
High-temperature or extreme-service testing can evaluate refractory behavior together with strength, ductility, and density.
Microstructural features and phase-stability indicators mediate the intrinsic mechanical properties of RHEAs.
The model exploits correlations between elemental characteristics and thermodynamic predictors.
Data-driven screening can rapidly identify compositions that balance multiple target properties.
The proposed approach bypasses labor-intensive parameter sweeps required by traditional methods.
Machine-learning-designed candidates will outperform conventionally designed candidates simultaneously in intrinsic strength, ductility, and low weight.
Thermo-kinetic analysis, CALPHAD, and high-throughput parameter sweeps are time-consuming and less efficient for exploring large composition spaces.
The effectiveness of the approach is limited by the quality and comprehensiveness of the available datasets.
Synthesis and processing challenges can change actual microstructures and properties relative to model predictions.
The magnitude of any performance improvement remains uncertain until experimental validation.
Data bias and prediction errors may affect the resulting alloy performance.
Failure to obtain statistically significant improvements in all three target properties relative to conventionally designed controls would refute the hypothesis.
